extracted.intended_audience: authors preparing randomized controlled trial (RCT) manuscripts for journal submission / clinical researchers reporting RCTs
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for how to write and structure manuscripts reporting parallel-group randomized controlled trials, covering title/abstract, introduction, methods, results, discussion, and other required information (registration, protocol, funding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification as a randomized trial in the title (Item 1a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Manuscript title should include the words 'randomized trial' to ensure correct indexing of the manuscript in electronic databases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including 'randomized trial' in the title ensures correct indexing and identification as a trial, enhances visibility, and may increase citation potential and research metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Structured summary in the abstract (Item 1b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Structured summary of trial design, methods, results, and conclusions in the abstract.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract should be structured, brief, and clear, presenting information found in the body. A well-written abstract is essential because readers often judge trial quality from it and it may be the only accessible source if the full report is not freely available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific background and rationale (Item 2a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the scientific background and explanation of the rationale for the trial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Introduction should set the scientific scene and explain why the trial was essential; for human-subject trials include ethical clearance and demonstration of potential benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific objectives or hypotheses (Item 2b)
rubrics_metrics.description: State the specific objectives or hypotheses the trial is intended to investigate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Objectives and hypotheses should be reported clearly in the Introduction so readers understand the trial's aims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of trial design (Item 3a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the trial design (such as parallel, factorial) including the allocation ratio.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methods must include detailed reporting of type of design (e.g., parallel group, factorial) and allocation ratio; CONSORT focuses mainly on randomized parallel group designs but requires explicit statement of design type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Important changes to methods after commencement (Item 3b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report important changes to methods after trial commencement (such as eligibility criteria), with reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any amendments to initial objectives or protocol during the trial should be transparently reported along with reasons to allow readers to interpret findings appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility criteria for participants (Item 4a)
rubrics_metrics.description: State eligibility criteria for participants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly defined eligibility criteria enable readers to interpret results and assess applicability; include any inclusion/exclusion specifics used in the protocol.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settings and locations (Item 4b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report settings and locations where the data were collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify county, city, hospital, clinic, and other contextual details as they impact study validity and generalizability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interventions sufficient for replication (Item 5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the interventions for each group with sufficient details to allow replication, including how and when they were actually administered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough detail about interventions (for drug trials: drug name, dose, mode of administration, timing, duration) so others can replicate the procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completely defined outcome measures (Item 6a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Completely define pre-specified primary and secondary outcome measures, including how and when they were assessed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Outcomes should be identified and defined in Methods so readers and future researchers can use the same outcomes and interpret findings consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes to trial outcomes after commencement (Item 6b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report any changes to trial outcomes after the trial commenced, with reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If outcomes were amended during the trial, these changes and justifications must be disclosed to avoid selective reporting bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sample size determination (Item 7a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the sample size was determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report the process of establishing an ethically and scientifically approved sample size, providing evidence of statistical power for the study population.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim analyses and stopping guidelines (Item 7b)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, explain any interim analyses and stopping guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If interim analyses or stopping rules were planned, describe them and their rationale to clarify potential impacts on study conduct and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Method of random allocation sequence generation (Item 8a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the method used to generate the random allocation sequence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient detail on sequence generation to evaluate randomization integrity (e.g., computer-generated, random number table).

rubrics_metrics.name: Type of randomization and restrictions (Item 8b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report the type of randomization and details of any restriction (such as blocking and block size).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify whether simple, blocked, stratified randomization was used and report blocking details to allow assessment of allocation balance and reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation concealment mechanism (Item 9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe the mechanism used to implement the random allocation sequence (such as sequentially numbered containers), including steps taken to conceal the sequence until interventions were assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail how allocation concealment was achieved to assess risk of selection bias (e.g., sealed envelopes, central randomization).

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation of randomization (Item 10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report who generated the random allocation sequence, who enrolled participants, and who assigned participants to interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarify roles and responsibilities in enrollment and assignment to demonstrate separation of duties and reduce bias risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Blinding (masking) (Item 11a)
rubrics_metrics.description: If done, state who was blinded after assignment to interventions (e.g., participants, care providers, outcome assessors) and how.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain blinding procedures, who was blinded, whether blinding was instituted from the start, and how it was maintained to allow assessment of performance and detection bias.

rubrics_metrics.name: Similarity of interventions (Item 11b)
rubrics_metrics.description: If relevant, describe the similarity of interventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When blinding depends on intervention similarity (e.g., placebo appearance), report details so readers can judge adequacy of blinding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical methods for primary and secondary outcomes (Item 12a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe statistical methods used to compare groups for primary and secondary outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide detailed descriptions of analyses planned and performed to allow replication and evaluation of appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for additional analyses (Item 12b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe methods for additional analyses, such as subgroup analyses and adjusted analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State which analyses were pre-specified versus exploratory and describe methods used for subgroup or adjusted analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant flow (diagram recommended) (Item 13a)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each group, give numbers of participants who were randomly assigned, who received intended treatment, and who were analyzed for the primary outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the CONSORT flowchart to illustrate participant progress through the trial; provide counts at each stage to clarify attrition and analysis denominators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Losses and exclusions after randomization (Item 13b)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each group, report losses and exclusions after randomization, together with reasons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detail reasons for loss to follow-up and exclusions to enable assessment of attrition bias and robustness of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment dates and follow-up periods (Item 14a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide dates defining the periods of recruitment and follow-up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting recruitment and follow-up periods helps contextualize results and potential temporal effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Why trial ended or stopped (Item 14b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain why the trial ended or was stopped.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the trial ended early or was stopped, report the reasons (e.g., futility, benefit, safety) as they affect interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Baseline demographic and clinical characteristics (Item 15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a table showing baseline demographic and clinical characteristics for each group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Baseline tables allow assessment of group comparability and potential confounding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Numbers analyzed and analysis denominator (Item 16)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each group, state number of participants (denominator) included in each analysis and whether analysis was by original assigned groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report per-protocol and/or intention-to-treat analyses and which participants were included to clarify analytic approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outcomes and estimation (effect sizes and precision) (Item 17a)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each primary and secondary outcome, present results for each group and the estimated effect size and its precision (such as 95% confidence interval).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide effect estimates with measures of precision to allow readers to judge clinical and statistical significance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation of absolute and relative effect sizes for binary outcomes (Item 17b)
rubrics_metrics.description: For binary outcomes, present both absolute and relative effect sizes (recommended).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing both absolute and relative measures improves interpretability of binary outcome results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ancillary analyses (Item 18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report results of any other analyses performed, including subgroup analyses and adjusted analyses, distinguishing pre-specified from exploratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clearly label analyses as pre-specified or exploratory to avoid overinterpretation of post-hoc findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Harms and unintended effects (Item 19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report all important harms or unintended effects in each group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe adverse events and harms; see CONSORT extension for harms for specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial limitations (Item 20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss trial limitations, addressing sources of potential bias, imprecision, and, if relevant, multiplicity of analyses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Discussion should include strengths and weaknesses and explicitly address biases and imprecision that could affect interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Generalizability (external validity) (Item 21)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss generalizability (external validity, applicability) of the trial findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how setting, participants, interventions, and other factors affect applicability to other populations or contexts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation consistent with results (Item 22)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide an interpretation consistent with results, balancing benefits and harms, and considering other relevant evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interpret findings in context, weigh benefits against harms, and relate results to existing literature and evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration (Item 23)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide registration number and name of trial registry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Register trials at the outset and include registry details in the manuscript to avoid patent/infringement issues and selective reporting; registration should occur at the beginning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol access (Item 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: State where the full trial protocol can be accessed, if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide location or link to full protocol so readers can review planned methods and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Funding and role of funders (Item 25)
rubrics_metrics.description: Report sources of funding and other support (such as the supply of drugs) and the role of funders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclose all funding sources and the funders' roles in study design, conduct, analysis, and reporting to allow readers to assess potential conflicts or influences.
